subject: Dedicated capacity planning for Atlas Retail - intake and next steps
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@atlasretail.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: Atlas Retail Platform Team <infra@atlasretail.com>
Date: 2028-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry - high-volume personalization API

Hi Chloe,

We spoke at the conference last month and I wanted to reach out about Dedicated capacity for a new personalization feature we're rolling into our checkout flow. We need predictable latency at scale and want to understand how Redwood would size a GPU pool for our workload.

High level context:
- Production traffic starting Q4, estimated 5M requests/day in month 1, plan to double over 6 months.
- Typical call: user profile + browsing context → prompt ~80 tokens, expected model response ~220 tokens.
- Target P95 end-to-end generation latency under 300ms for the majority of requests; some heavier context paths can tolerate 600ms.
- We prefer an open model family and want to explore quantized variants.

Can you share a short questionnaire or checklist we can fill so your sizing team can provide a preliminary footprint? Also interested in burst handling and autoscaling options.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Platform
Atlas Retail

Attachments: none
From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: Elena Park <elena@atlasretail.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry - high-volume personalization API

Hi Elena,

Great to hear from you — thanks for the context. I've attached our lightweight dedicated sizing questionnaire that captures traffic shape, concurrency, prompt/response token distributions, and SLO targets. If you can fill that out it will let us produce a preliminary GPU fleet sketch (SKU mix, baseline concurrency, and burst runway).

Key things that help our sizing team:
- Peak RPS (5/95 minute windows) and typical daily shape (UTC).
- Percent of calls that require long-context retrieval or multi-turn session affinity.
- Whether you need persistent KV cache/streaming and expected session duration.
- Preferred model family (we can size for both FP16 and 4-bit quantized variants).

Proposed next step: you fill the attached spreadsheet and I’ll loop Marissa (solutions) and Laura (pre-sales infra) for a 30–45m sizing review. I blocked 30m Thursday morning but happy to shift.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Pre-Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_questionnaire_v2.xlsx (questionnaire template)
From: Elena Park <elena@atlasretail.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: Atlas Retail Platform Team <infra@atlasretail.com>
Date: 2028-05-22T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry - high-volume personalization API

Hi Chloe,

Thanks — attached is our completed intake (atlas_dedicated_questionnaire_filled.xlsx) and a small CSV with a week of sampled token counts (atlas_token_profile_sample.csv). A few clarifications inline in the sheet, but summary below:

Summarized inputs:
- Baseline daily requests: 5,000,000/day (UTC), 95th-minute peak ~12,000 RPS, typical baseline 2,800 RPS.
- Prompt length distribution: median 65 tokens, 90th 140 tokens.
- Response length distribution: median 180 tokens, 95th 420 tokens.
- ~18% of calls require user-profile lookup + 2 retrieval documents (adds ~120 tokens to prompt).
- Session affinity: light (stateless) except for review flows (~3% of calls) that keep a session for ~45s.
- Streaming: desired for large responses (yes).
- Model: leaning toward a 4-bit quantized Llama-3 class variant; willing to pilot FP16 for P95 SLOs.

We noted the desire for a P95 <300ms — open to discussing a fall-back routing policy for best-effort lower-cost variants during extreme bursts.

Thanks,
Elena

Attachments: atlas_dedicated_questionnaire_filled.xlsx, atlas_token_profile_sample.csv
From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Park <elena@atlasretail.com>
Date: 2028-05-23T10:17:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity inquiry - Atlas Retail - intake attached

Team — forwarding Atlas' completed intake. Key numbers: 5M/day, 95m peak ~12k RPS, median prompt 65 / median resp 180, ~18% retrieval calls, streaming required. Customer target: P95 <300ms, occasional tolerance up to 600ms. They prefer quantized Llama-3 class but will pilot FP16.

Questions for sizing:
- For the 12k RPS 95m peak, what's the recommended SKU mix and baseline headroom for 2-minute sustained peaks?
- With ~18% retrieval adds, should we recommend a separate retrieval-optimized pool (smaller context kernels) or size a single pool with a mixed workload profile?
- Suggested autoscale/burst policy thresholds and recommended queue/backpressure settings to preserve P95 SLOs.

Elena, looping Marissa and Laura to propose a preliminary footprint and a 45m review slot. Available: Friday 09:00-12:00 PT or Monday 10:00-14:00 PT.

-Chloe
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Park <elena@atlasretail.com>
Date: 2028-05-24T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity inquiry - Atlas Retail - intake attached

Thanks for the intake — quick preliminary thinking below; I’ll follow up with a short pdf with a recommended SKU mix and ops playbook.

Prelim sizing notes (very rough):
- For 12k RPS 95m peak and average token mix (prompt+response ~245 tokens), using a 4-bit quantized Llama-3 class, expect ~0.018 GPU-seconds per request on an optimized kernel (ballpark). That suggests ~216 GPU-seconds/s sustained at 12k RPS which maps to ~8.6 A100-class GPU equivalents for the peak sustained window. Recommend baseline pool of 12 GPUs (quantized-capable) to provide headroom and autoscale runway, with 6 additional burst GPUs reserved for emergency overflow (or use on-demand dedicated burst).
- Retrieval calls are heavier (longer context) — better to route to a small separate retrieval pool tuned for long-context kernels (4 GPUs) to avoid P99 blowups on the general pool.
- Autoscale policy: scale-up at sustained 80% utilization over 60s, scale-down after 5 mins below 50%. Queueing: prefer short tail latency preservation via a hard concurrency cap per worker and 5-second client-side retry guidance.
- For P95 <300ms, pilot FP16 variants for hot routes (review flows) and keep quantized for bulk traffic; fallback routing in extreme bursts.

Next steps: I will prepare a 2-page footprint PDF and a recommended canary + rollout plan. Elena — are you okay to meet Friday 11:00 AM PT for a 45m walkthrough?

- Marissa

Attachments referenced: redwood_prelim_sizing_notes.pdf
